messages:
Maria V.: Quick sync — we need cross-team agreement on a small set of metrics for continuous-batching dashboards. Runtime/infra inputs required: batch_size distribution, batch_wait percentiles, fill_rate, and a saturation indicator. Thoughts?

Owen C.: +1. Recommend p50/p90/p99 for wait_ms and batch_size. Also we should expose model + deployment labels so product can slice by customer.

Kevin L.: From infra side: prefer a namespaced pattern like `inference_batch_size_bucket` (histogram) and `inference_batch_wait_seconds_bucket`. Keep labels minimal: model, deployment, region, instance_shard. No request-level ids. We'll emit buckets up to 128.

Sunita R.: Product asks to show both "customer-visible latency" (end-to-end) and internal queue wait. We'll need two rows: E2E latency (existing) and batch-wait breakdown (new).

Maria V.: Good. For the dashboard I propose these panels: 
- Heatmap: batch_size distribution over time (histogram -> heatmap).
- Line: batch_size p50/p90/p99 (rolling 5m).
- Fill-rate: percentage of batch slots actually filled (p95).
- Saturation: queued_requests / capacity as ratio with warn at 0.7, critical at 0.85.

Owen C.: For alerts: saturation_ratio > 0.85 for 5m -> page oncall. Also low fill-rate + increased p99 wait -> early warning.

Julia M.: I'll take dashboard layout in Grafana. Can you paste example queries we can wire?

Maria V.: Example PromQLs: 
```
# p90 batch wait by model
histogram_quantile(0.9, sum(rate(inference_batch_wait_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, model, deployment))

# batch size heatmap source
sum(rate(inference_batch_size_bucket[5m])) by (le, model)

# fill rate (slots_filled / slots_available)
sum(rate(inference_batch_slots_filled_total[5m])) by (model) / sum(rate(inference_batch_slots_available_total[5m])) by (model)

# saturation ratio
sum(inference_queued_requests_total) by (deployment) / sum(inference_capacity_slots_total) by (deployment)
```

Rahul S.: Runtime note: we can't natively emit a 2D histogram. Best option is emit size and wait histograms with identical bucket boundaries + same labels. Grafana can combine them into a heatmap approximation. We'll also include an invariant label `batch_shape_version` so infra knows the schema.

Kevin L.: We need cardinality guardrails. Proposal: default scrape turns off `instance_shard` label unless `enable_shard_metrics=true` on specific deployments. Also limit `model` cardinality by mapping customers -> logical_model when >X models.

Sunita R.: Also: routing policies affect batch shapes (fallback vs primary path). Can runtime add `routing_policy` label with values `primary|fallback|low_cost`? Product wants to compare.

Maria V.: Yes please add `routing_policy`. Action item for runtime: emit metrics with labels (model, deployment, region, routing_policy, batch_shape_version).

Owen C.: Infra action items: build dashboard skeleton + alert rules in `observability/alerts/batching/`. Can we also add a compact SLO-oriented panel that shows expected throughput vs actual? When quotas throttle the expected_throughput will diverge.

Julia M.: I'll open PR for dashboard skeleton. Link: https://github.com/redwood/infra/pull/1427 (WIP) :point_right: will add panels and variable templates.

devops-bot: metric-agent v2.4 deployed to canaries at 2026-02-15T10:15Z. New histogram export toggle enabled. :rocket:

Kevin L.: One more ask — annotate dashboard with rollout tags so when Dedicated vs Hosted differs we can toggle. Use `deployment=hosted|dedicated` label.

Maria V.: Timeline check: runtime to emit test metrics by EOD Wed (2026-02-18), infra to land dashboard skeleton by Thu, product to validate panels by Fri. I'll schedule a 20m async review. :calendar:

Rahul S.: I'll push a small test payload generator to emit synthetic batch_size/wait histograms so Grafana panels have data. PR incoming.

Owen C.: Sounds good. If anyone needs mock queries or bucket boundaries, ping me. :thumbsup:

Julia M.: Opening PR now and will drop screenshot when panels wired.

Sunita R.: Thanks all — this should make routing/quota UX far easier to debug.

Maria V.: Thanks — closing this thread once PRs are linked and test metrics are confirmed.
